original_question: For the Dirichlet-type spaces D^alpha with alpha < 0 and alpha != -1, determine the extremal quantity M, where M is the infimum of |z| over zeros of optimal polynomial approximants q_{n,f} of 1/f, and determine the corresponding extremal function. Equivalently, for alpha < 0 and alpha != -1, determine the norm of the Jacobi matrix J with entries J_{ij} = sqrt((j+1)^alpha / (j+2)^alpha) when |i-j| = 1 and J_{ij} = 0 otherwise.
target_in_paper: Open Question 1 in §4.1 (“One variable spaces”), together with the immediately preceding discussion of Theorem 4.1, where the survey isolates the unsolved Dirichlet-type case α < 0, α ≠ -1 and rephrases it as a Jacobi-matrix norm problem.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the relevant parameter range α < 0 with α ≠ -1, the minimal-zero/extremal problem for optimal polynomial approximants to 1/f in Dirichlet-type spaces, the need to identify an extremal function, and the paper’s equivalent Jacobi-matrix reformulation.
missing_details: The ambient space should be defined explicitly: D_α = {f(z) = Σ_{k≥0} a_k z^k on the unit disk 𝔻 : ‖f‖_α^2 = Σ_{k≥0} (k+1)^α |a_k|^2 < ∞}.
The infimum must be quantified over all orders n ≥ 1, all functions f ∈ D_α with f(0) ≠ 0, and all zeros of the corresponding optimal polynomial approximants.
q_{n,f} should be defined as the unique polynomial of degree at most n minimizing ‖qf - 1‖_α among all polynomials q of degree at most n.
The exact meaning of “extremal function” should be stated: a function in D_α for which the minimal-zero infimum is attained.
The paper’s surrounding discussion makes clear that, in this regime, the infimum is actually a minimum; your draft does not state that attainment is part of the problem.
The relation between the two formulations should be stated explicitly: if J_α is the associated Jacobi matrix, then the minimal modulus satisfies M_α = 2/‖J_α‖.

The Jacobi matrix needs an unambiguous indexing convention and operator domain; equivalently one can specify it by its zero diagonal and off-diagonal entries (2/3)^{α/2}, (3/4)^{α/2}, (4/5)^{α/2}, … acting on ℓ²(ℕ₀).
To stay paper-faithful, it helps to note that α = -1 is excluded because that case is already explicitly solved in the literature surveyed there.
refined_question: For the Dirichlet-type space D_α = {f(z) = Σ_{k≥0} a_k z^k : ‖f‖_α^2 := Σ_{k≥0} (k+1)^α |a_k|^2 < ∞} on the unit disk 𝔻, with α < 0 and α ≠ -1, let q_{n,f} denote the n-th optimal polynomial approximant to 1/f, i.e. the unique polynomial of degree at most n minimizing ‖qf - 1‖_α among all polynomials q of degree at most n, for f ∈ D_α with f(0) ≠ 0. Determine the exact value of M_α := inf{|z| : q_{n,f}(z) = 0 for some n ≥ 1 and some f ∈ D_α with f(0) ≠ 0}, and identify an extremal function f_α^* ∈ D_α for which this minimum is attained.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, determine the operator norm of the infinite Jacobi matrix J_α on ℓ²(ℕ₀) with zero diagonal and off-diagonal entries (2/3)^{α/2}, (3/4)^{α/2}, (4/5)^{α/2}, …; then M_α = 2/‖J_α‖.
justification: This draft is targeting the survey’s Open Question 1 in §4.1, not a broader neighboring topic. In §4.1 the paper recalls the “minimal-zero” problem through Theorem 4.1, which is exactly the infimum over moduli of zeros of optimal polynomial approximants, and it states the Dirichlet-type dichotomy showing that the α < 0 regime is the one where zeros may enter the unit disk. Immediately afterward, the survey singles out the still-unsolved subcase α < 0, α ≠ -1, asks for the corresponding extremal function, and explicitly rephrases the problem as computing the norm of the associated Jacobi matrix. The introduction and §2 provide the definitions of the spaces D_α and of the optimal polynomial approximants q_{n,f}, so those definitions have to be folded into the refined stand-alone question.
